A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SALSA-V. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, model ablations, conditioning and duration analyses, qualitative examples, and an 18-participant listening study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, generation-time measurements, and evaluation of a 1.01B-parameter variant.

M1.justification: The masked latent flow-matching model, synchronization encoder, shortcut objective, and inference procedure are retained. Explicit mask-sampling and shortcut-target descriptions document existing components; the larger-model experiment does not establish a new algorithm or architectural component.

E1.justification: The training and evaluation data sources remain unchanged, as do ordinary video-to-audio generation, audio conditioning, and long-form generation coverage. The new four-step and 30-second comparisons fall within scenarios already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the objective comparison from FoleyCrafter and MMAudio to also include Frieren, V-AURA, LoVA, and AudioX. v2 additionally evaluates Frieren's reflow checkpoint in the few-step comparison and LoVA in the dedicated long-form comparison. The human-study comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a common-hardware timing protocol using an NVIDIA A100, batch size 1, and 10-second outputs; matched four-step and 30-second comparisons; and a 1.01B model configuration. The established training settings, quality metrics, and listening-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 and Appendix A.7 extend the existing model-size analysis beyond 347M and 643M parameters to 1.01B. The flow-matching versus shortcut ablation, sampling-budget and duration analyses, conditioning-length analysis, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged. Existing shaded plot bands remain without newly supplied explanations, seed counts, repeated-run protocols, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The listening study still reports 18 participants completing 10 trials each.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 rows and Table 2 values are retained, but substantial results are added in Tables 1 and 3–6. AudioX now has the lowest KLPANNs value, 1.70, and ties SALSA-V's KLPaSST of 1.63. New results include matched Frieren and LoVA comparisons, runtime measurements, and the 1.01B variant's FAD of 1.05 and DeSync of 0.486; these are added comparisons and configurations, not improvements to the unchanged original model results.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds explicit definitions of the EMA-based shortcut target and intermediate Euler step in Equations 3–4; v1 leaves the target implicit. No proofs or broader theoretical results are added. The second target term uses time t with the intermediate latent indexed t+d, leaving an apparent time-index ambiguity.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about synchronized generation, masked audio conditioning and long-form extension, and efficient shortcut sampling without dedicated retraining. The shortened conclusion and additional experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the larger-model results as evidence of favorable scaling and adds discussion of applications and media-manipulation risks. It removes v1's explicit acknowledgment of inferior subjective audio quality despite retaining the same human scores. The limitation concerning scene cuts during progressive outpainting remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies uniform sampling of mask lengths and center positions, including boundary coverage, and identifies EMA parameters as the source of shortcut targets. It supplies hardware and batch settings for runtime measurements. The existing appendix training details and project access link remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds brief discussions of SpecVQGAN, Seeing and Hearing, MDSGen, TARO, and PAVAS; AudioX is also newly cited. This broadens related-work coverage while retaining the existing novelty framing. Updates to publication years and venues for previously cited works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include localized methodological explanations, an expanded related-work subsection, a shorter conclusion, new impact and acknowledgment sections, and an Audio Conditioning appendix subsection. Figure references replace previously unhelpful references back to Section 4.1.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 expands and Tables 3–6 are added. Figure 1 gains color coding and an expanded caption; the turkey-conditioning example moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 5, while the existing performance curves become Figure 4. Appendix figures are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for two central contributions: Table 3 compares few-step quality against Frieren's reflow checkpoint, Table 5 tests long-form generation against LoVA, and Table 4 supplies actual common-hardware latency measurements. These address important comparative and efficiency-evidence gaps in v1. Removing the audio-quality limitation despite unchanged MOS values of 2.96 versus MMAudio's 3.16 weakens balance, and the added target equation has a time-index ambiguity. Those shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
